info.text:
By default, a one-owner LLC cuts your federal taxes by $0.

The IRS treats a single-member LLC as a disregarded entity: same Schedule C, same 15.3% self-employment tax as a sole proprietor.
Example: $50,000 of profit x 92.35% x 15.3% = about $7,065 either way.
The Social Security part is capped at $184,500 for 2026 and $192,300 for 2027 (SSA).
What changes: a state-law liability shield for business debts (not your own negligence or personal guarantees), state fees (California: $800 a year), and an optional S corp election (Form 2553).

Sources: IRS Publication 3402, IRS Topic 554, SSA, California Franchise Tax Board.
News and education, not financial advice.
